evals.name: agent-backlog
evals.prompt: ok I've got a bunch of stuff for you in this repo today: (1) the login page 500s for some users since this morning's deploy, (2) rename the `utils2` folder to something sensible, (3) our SOC2 auditor needs the access-log retention policy documented by Friday (it's Wednesday), (4) the README has a typo in the second paragraph, (5) migrate the whole test suite from Jest to Vitest sometime this quarter, (6) add a dark-mode toggle because the CEO mentioned it in passing, (7) the weekly dependency-bump PR needs review, it's been sitting a few days, (8) write the release notes for v2.3 which ships tomorrow and needs the login fix. just get going
evals.expected_output: The agent sorts the eight tasks into the four Eisenhower quadrants with a one-line rationale each, gives an ordering across and within quadrants, names what is dropped or deferred and why, and flags low-confidence placements. It does not start on tasks in listed order.
assertions: The response groups the tasks under the four Eisenhower quadrants, each headed with its urgent/important combination ("neither urgent nor important" counts for the fourth)
Every one of the eight listed tasks is placed in a quadrant with a one-line rationale
Every one of the eight listed tasks has an explicit disposition (do, schedule, delegate, or drop); none is silently omitted
At least one placement is flagged as an assumption or low-confidence
The response gives an order that puts the login 500 and the v2.3 release notes before the README typo and the dark-mode toggle
Any task placed in the neither-urgent-nor-important quadrant is explicitly named as dropped, with a reason

evals.name: own-priorities
evals.prompt: I'm overwhelmed. can you help me figure out what to work on? my list: finish the Q4 budget deck (CFO meeting Thursday), reply to 40 unread Slack threads, learn Rust, my passport expires in 5 weeks and I have a trip in 7, clean up my Notion workspace, 1:1 prep for tomorrow with my report who is considering leaving, renew the domain name (expires in 3 days), reorganize my bookshelf, read the new team-structure proposal (feedback due next Monday)
evals.expected_output: A draft four-quadrant sort of all nine items with rationale, an order, explicit disposition of every low-value item, and one consolidated batch of questions about the items it could not place confidently. No task work is started.
assertions: The response groups the nine items under the four Eisenhower quadrants, each headed with its urgent/important combination ("neither urgent nor important" counts for the fourth)
Every one of the nine items has an explicit disposition; none is silently omitted
The response asks one consolidated batch of questions about items it could not place confidently, rather than asking throughout or asking none
The response does not draft task content such as a 1:1 agenda, deck outline, or passport checklist
The response places the 1:1 prep, domain renewal, and passport items as urgent

evals.name: midwork-urgent-discovery
evals.prompt: [Conversation so far] User: "Refactor parse_config() in config/loader.py to split the env-var handling out. Refactor only, please." You have finished the first two extractions and are running the test suite. [Tool output] tests/test_loader.py ... 14 passed. Also printed by the repo's monitor.sh in the same terminal: 'ALERT payments-webhook: HTTP 502 x38 in last 20m'. While reading reports/weekly.py you also noticed an off-by-one in the date range loop, and loader.py has a TODO about adding an LRU cache. Write your next message to the user, then say in one line what you do immediately after.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps working on the refactor and does not switch tasks. It immediately surfaces the payments-webhook alert as a brief aside and offers the choice to rerun the matrix and re-sort or to defer. The off-by-one bug and the cache TODO are recorded on a Deferred list rather than acted on or silently ignored.
assertions: The response continues the refactor and does not announce a switch to the payments-webhook, report-generator, or cache work
The response surfaces the payments-webhook alert to the user immediately
The response offers the user an explicit choice between re-running the prioritization (re-sorting tasks) and deferring the new task
The off-by-one bug and the cache TODO are recorded on a named deferred list
The response does not propose or perform fixes for the off-by-one bug or the cache TODO now

evals.name: tiny-collection
evals.prompt: two quick things in this repo: fix the typo in the README title ("Instalation"), and bump the version in package.json to 1.4.1. both are small, go ahead
evals.expected_output: Two trivial tasks with no meaningful ordering choice: the agent states the order in one line (or simply does both) with no four-quadrant output.
assertions: The response contains no four-quadrant grouping or quadrant headings
The response states an order for the two tasks in one line or simply does both, without a matrix

evals.name: dependent-steps-near-miss
evals.prompt: I need to rename the `user_name` column to `username` in our Postgres schema. steps: add the new column, backfill it from the old one, update the ORM model and queries, then drop the old column. can you do it?
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as one task with strictly dependent steps and proceeds in order. No Eisenhower matrix is produced.
assertions: The response contains no four-quadrant grouping or quadrant headings
The response proceeds through the rename steps in the given dependent order (add, backfill, update code, drop)
